title: Space bound from bounded computation segments
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\\{0,1\\}$ with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $(c_j)_{j\\in\\mathbb N}$ be configurations of $M$ on $x$. Suppose $N,B,H,$ and $r$ are natural numbers with $r\\le B$, the computation from the initial configuration reaches $c_0$ after $r$ steps, and for every $j<N$ and every tape the head position in $c_j$ lies between $-H$ and $H$. Suppose also that $c_N$ is halted, its tape-head positions lie between $-(H+B)$ and $H+B$, and for each $j<N$ there is a $u\\le B$ such that the run from $c_j$ is halted after $u$ steps or reaches $c_{j+1}$ after $u$ steps. Then, for every $t\\in\\mathbb N$, the total space used from the initial configuration through step $t$ is at most $k(2(H+B)+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$(c_j)$ is a sequence of configurations on $x$
The run from the initial configuration reaches $c_0$ after $r$ steps
For every $j<N$, every tape head in $c_j$ lies in $[-H,H]$
Every tape head in $c_N$ lies in $[-(H+B),H+B]$
For every $j<N$, some $u\\le B$ makes the run from $c_j$ halt or reach $c_{j+1}$
